messages.subject: Operative temperatures at different heights
parts:
Hi Everyone!

I am picking back up my global, multi species, long-term operative temperature project again. I have things mostly done, but now want to include an operative temp for each species at the ground level and at a height of about 2m. I know I can just run the microclimate model twice and change the value of my local height, but micro_ncep takes a super long time to run, and I really don't want to double the amount of time. If that is my only option then that is fine, but I was not sure if there was another quicker way to obtain the two different body temps.

Thanks for the help!
-Julie

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Operative temperatures at different heights
parts:
Hi Julie,

To speed things up you could try downloading the NCEP data locally - there are details in previous conversations in this Google Group about it. But either way, you only need to run the microclimate model once, and then modify the microclimate inputs prior to running the ectotherm model. E.g. if you wanted to set local air temp to the 2 m reference value, you could do this:

micro$metout[, 3] <- micro$metout[, 4]

because column 3 is TALOC and column 4 is TAREF. You could do the same for wind speed and humidity, and for the shaded microclimate (shadmet) too. Note that by default the ectotherm model looks for e.g. micro$metout, micro$soil, micro$shadmet
as the microclimate inputs, just to make it easy to run so that you have less code to write. But you can pass it different, modified microclimate inputs, e.g. to set up a metabolic chamber example, as long as it's in the same tabular structure.

So I'd suggest you do something like this:

micro <- micro_ncep( ....)
ecto <- ectotherm( ...) # run the ectotherm model at the specified local height

micro_original <- micro # make a copy of the original version in case you need it
micro$metout[, 3] <- micro$metout[, 4]
micro$metout[, 5] <- micro$metout[, 5]  .... etc.
ecto <- ectotherm( ...) # run the ectotherm model using the modified micro output list

All the best,
Mike
